title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 7 Primo: elect cannot lose crown — certainty from causal chain, not bare foresight
pass_a_gloss: First: the predestined cannot lose the crown of glory; yet this certainty of obtaining the crown does not arise from a necessity that forces them to eternal life, nor does it rest on bare divine foreknowledge looking at what they will do from their free will; but it is founded in that order of causes which a certain special Divine providence has chained together for infallibly producing the salvation of the elect. This certainty — not of bare foresight, but of causality — the Apostle indicated in Romans 8, where he teaches that God has so instituted and governs the order of causes for advancing the elect's salvation that even those things which seem hostile to their salvation nevertheless work together for them unto the eternal good of their souls; verse 28 and following to the end of the chapter.
pass_b_english: First: the predestined cannot lose the crown of glory. That certainty does not come from a force that drags them into eternal life, nor from bare foresight of what free will will do. It rests on the chain of causes special providence has linked so the elect's salvation is produced without fail. Paul marks that as causality, not naked foresight — Romans 8: God so set and steers the order of causes for the elect that even what looks hostile still works for their souls' eternal good (vv. 28ff to the chapter's end).
source_text: Primo, Non posse praedestinatos amittere coronam gloriae: hanc tamen certitudinem adipiscendi coronam non oriri ex necessitate cogente illos ad vitam aeternam, neque niti mera Dei praescientia intuente quid illi ex libero suo arbitrio facturi sint; sed fundatam esse in illo causarum ordine quem specialis quaedam Divina providentia ad salutem electorum infallibiliter producendam concatenavit. Hanc certitudinem, non nudae praescientiae, sed causalitatis Apostolus indicavit Rom. viii. ubi docet ita Deum instituisse & gubernare ordinem causarum ad promovendam salutem electorum, ut omnia etiam illa quae saluti illorum infesta videntur, tamen cooperentur illis in aeternum bonum animarum; versu 28. & seq. usque ad finem capitis.
